name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, the design-driver pattern: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.19.0 — a review that burns its fix loop to the cap (2 iterations) and is then abandoned no longer writes zero ledger rows: the cap refusal now appends an **escalate row** at the moment of the refusal, an honestly-derived non-CLEAN verdict carrying `escalated: true`, minted by `verdict.js` behind a new `--escalated` flag with `--fixDispatched 0` (the dispatched fix never landed; refused with `--fixDispatched > 0` or `--profile release`, and refused rather than printed when the derivation reaches CLEAN under evidence drift — a self-contradictory CLEAN+escalated row is the worst possible output the one file that must never wrongly say CLEAN could carry). `spec-review-driver.js`'s `writeEscalateRow()` runs the pass from `handleFixApplied()`'s cap branch before dying, reusing spec 04's stopped-ledger durability verbatim in a worktree (`<mainRoot>/.claude/spec-runs.stopped.jsonl`, drained into the tracked ledger at close positioned before the close row) and self-healing a missing append on a bare re-invocation via the sidecar's `escalateRunId` mark. The ESCALATE step text now names both exits — fresh dispositions (`--fix-dispatched 0` covering the pool) closing normally through the waive/reject route, or deleting the `<spec>.review/` sidecar to abandon and restart cold — plus the absolute path the row landed in; a new driver-entry detector warns (stderr-only, never blocking) when a sidecar-recorded durable path no longer has a readable row for the spec+runId. `spec/commands/review.md`'s ledger-append sentence now names ESCALATE alongside STOPPED and CLOSE, and its ESCALATE re-entrancy prose names the row and both exits. No new verdict word: the escalation fact rides as a typed row field, never a second place that derives or asserts CLEAN. 7.18.0 — a foreign test's skip line now maps through to the owning spec's `[env:]` sanction on the realistic path: `ac-matrix.js` gains a third mapping route, tried only after both existing routes miss, that reads the runner's own file qualifier off a `<relpath>::<name>` skip line and takes that file's full-token AC-ID citations as `mappedIds`, feeding the existing sanction logic unchanged; every edge (no qualifier, path outside root, missing file, zero citations) fails closed to today's `unmapped-skip`, and `spec-review-driver.js`'s SKIPS prompt now instructs qualifier retention so the route has evidence to read. `smoke.sh` adds a pre-boot staleness probe: if `readyCheck` already passes before `bootCommand` is spawned, it prints `__SMOKE_FAIL__ stale-ready` naming the remedy and exits a new documented code 7 instead of booting into an environment it can't attribute readiness to (previously observed as exit 143 / `shutdown-unclean` when an orphaned prior process faked instant readiness). Separately, D5's reopen condition from 20260817/05 fired: `ac-matrix.js`'s coverage grep and `red-check.js`'s carried-AC classifier both did bare-substring AC-ID matching, so `AC-…-1` phantom-matched inside `AC-…-12` — coverage failed OPEN (4 laundered ACs across a 78-spec scan) and red-check failed CLOSED (a false `unsanctioned-green` that stopped specs/20260822/02's build same-day). Both call sites now go through one exported `lib/spec-sections.js` helper, `acIdOccurs(text, id)` — full-token by boundary check, no per-call RegExp — so a prefix hit neither launders coverage nor stops a build; the four historically-laundered ACs get `/spec:escape` rows against their owning reviews as separate recorded audit work, not silent repair. 7.17.0 — build's red-check (Phase 0 step 2's expected-colour classification plus Phase 1's hand-run reconciliation paragraph) is now mechanized by `spec/scripts/red-check.js` (`spec-paths red-check`), replacing prose with executed exit codes: expectation derives from `SHALL CONTINUE TO` pins and a new closed-enum `[pre-green: <reason>]` AC tag (`fallback-rejection` | `absence-invariant` | `predicate-in-test` — the three recorded sub-shapes of the class this spec closes); the script executes the host's own `{testCommand}`/`{typecheckCommand}` once per tests-layer file and reads exit codes only, never runner output, probing non-DELETE File Plan paths for existence before invoking the runner (a missing file would otherwise fake a satisfied red expectation) and refusing at exit 2 when any non-tests File Plan path already differs from the diff base, tracked or untracked. `lib/spec-sections.js`'s `parseAcBullets` gains the `preGreen` field and exports `PRE_GREEN_REASONS` as the single enum authority; `ac-matrix.js` counts valid tags into its typed manifest row (`observed.preGreen`) so the class rides every review ledger row fleet-countable, and rejects an out-of-enum reason as hard finding `invalid-pre-green` — the tag never launders coverage (a tagged AC with zero test hits still counts uncovered). The pipeline rules' thrice-amended vacuous-pin Gotchas paragraph (six recorded instances since 2026-08-17) shrinks to a one-line pointer at the script's incident header and its test file (JJ approved 2026-08-21). Deliberately NOT built (D12, rejected per core § Incident Policy): a mandatory per-AC mutation/kill-check — the class it would guard has zero recorded members across every ledger this repo can read, and `/spec:replay` already occupies that niche at a fraction of the cost; the tag remains a planner/worker attestation welded to execution, never a proof that the pinned assertion discriminates, which stays reviewer residue.
